about.title: Willits Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Willits is a small city, but the products people use here — from tools and vehicle parts to household appliances and equipment used on local ranches and farms — come from the same manufacturing and retail chains found everywhere else in California. When one of those products fails, whether through a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the injuries can be serious and the responsible party isn't always obvious. That's where a claim gets complicated: was it the maker, the distributor, or the store that sold it? California law lets injured people pursue the whole chain. LawProactive is a free connection service — not a law firm — and we can put you in touch with an independent attorney near Willits who reviews these cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered. If you were hurt, keep the product exactly as it was at the time of the incident and reach out to get matched with someone who can evaluate what happened.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Law

items.title: Strict Liability Can Apply
items.desc: California often allows product liability claims under strict liability, meaning you may not need to prove the manufacturer was careless — just that the product was defective and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all share liability, which matters in a place like Willits where products often pass through several hands before reaching a home or worksite.

items.title: The Product Itself Is Evidence
items.desc: Under California law, preserving the defective product in its post-incident condition is critical, since it's often the strongest evidence available to establish what went wrong.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims frequently rely on strict liability, which focuses on whether the product itself was defective and caused your injury rather than on the manufacturer's conduct. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your case to see which legal theory fits best.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was after the incident, including any packaging, parts, or instructions, and avoid repairing or altering it. This is one of the most important steps you can take, since the physical product is often central to proving a defect claim.

items.question: Is this common in a small city like Willits?
items.answer: Willits sees relatively few reported injury collisions each year, but product-related injuries can happen anywhere products are sold or used, whether that's along Main Street, S Main Street, or out on Rt 101 and Rt 20. Local size doesn't change the underlying California law that applies to defective product claims.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover money.
